title: The Death of Marat
source: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, Brussels, inv. 3260 (public domain). caption: A revolutionary in his bath, a letter in his hand, and a crime scene that was carefully staged. #frenchrevolution #truecrime #jacqueslouisdavid #arthistory #hiddendetails
_verify: VERIFIED 2026-10-24, Wikipedia EN (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Death_of_Marat): murder 13 July 1793 by Charlotte Corday, a Girondin who blamed Marat for the September Massacres; skin condition kept him in his bath, where he worked; often compared to Michelangelo's Pietà (hanging arm) and Caravaggio's Entombment; original in Brussels, studio replica in the Louvre; 162 x 128 cm.

VERIFIED 2026-10-24, BBC Culture 2025-10-28 (bbc.com/culture/article/20251028-the-death-of-marat-unlocking-the-complex-clues..., read via a mirror): Corday's letter 'It is enough that I am very unhappy', a ploy to exploit his kindness; Marat's own unfinished note pledging money to 'that mother of five children whose husband died in defence of the fatherland', held down by an assignat; signed 'To Marat, David' (A MARAT, DAVID) and dated 'l'an deux'; dangling arm echoes Christ in the Pietà and the Entombment; knife on the floor.

VERIFIED 2026-10-24, Mental Floss (mentalfloss.com/article/64750/...): David shows Marat 'free of such superficial flaws' (no skin disease); excludes the killer almost completely, she appears only in writing; reproductions made for propaganda; David was Marat's friend. Google Arts & Culture (artsandculture.google.com/asset/7QGjl9R141MCBw): the National Convention asked David to paint Marat; 'political propaganda opportunities' of the assassination.

VERIFIED 2026-10-24, Alpha History (alphahistory.com/frenchrevolution/charlotte-corday/): Corday executed 17 July 1793, four days after the murder; she called Marat 'a monster'. (Alpha History says she got in by claiming information on Girondin fugitives; the letter ploy is from BBC/Wikipedia. Slide 3 says only that she used his kindness to get in.)

CAUTIOUS: 'kitchen knife' (Eclectic Light 2025, BBC); slide 4 says only 'a knife'. The wound is not described or zoomed on; slide 6 box (head and arm) may include the chest in a wide frame, keep it wide.
CAUTIOUS: 'Half the canvas is empty darkness' is my description of the composition (upper half dark wall), not a sourced quote.

slides.headline: This crime scene was staged. Look closer.
slides.sub: Jacques-Louis David, The Death of Marat, 1793

slides.headline: Paris, July 1793
slides.text: Paris, July 1793. Jean-Paul Marat, firebrand of the Revolution, works in his bath to soothe a painful skin disease. Then a visitor arrives.

slides.headline: Her letter
slides.text: Look at his left hand. Her note pleads: "It is enough that I am very unhappy…" Charlotte Corday used his kindness to get in.

slides.headline: On the floor
slides.text: Minutes later, she struck. Yet David leaves her out: only her name on the letter and a knife on the floor remain.

slides.headline: Meanwhile, on the box
slides.text: Meanwhile, on the wooden box: a banknote and his unfinished note, pledging money to a war widow, mother of five. Generous to the end?

slides.headline: Too perfect
slides.text: But look at his skin: flawless. David, his friend, erased the disease, and the hanging arm echoes Christ carried to the tomb.

slides.headline: Signed like a tombstone
slides.text: And then the signature, like an epitaph: "To Marat, David." Dated Year Two of the Revolution, a whole new calendar.

slides.headline: The empty dark
slides.text: Above him, half the canvas is empty darkness. The Convention asked for this image, and copies spread it as propaganda: a revolutionary martyr.

slides.headline: Martyr or monster?
slides.text: Corday went to the guillotine four days later. To her, Marat was a monster. So tell us: martyr or monster? Who was the victim?
